**1. Observation‑schedule design** | Shift | Typical nurse coverage (assumption) | % of unit staff | # observations/month | Auditor(s) | |-------|-------------------------------------|-----------------|----------------------|------------| | Morning (08:00–16:00) | 11 nurses | 34 % | 14 | Auditor A | | Evening (16:00–24:00) | 10 nurses | 31 % | 13 | Auditor B | | Night (24:00–08:00) | 11 nurses | 35 % | 13 | Auditor A | *Assumptions:* - The three shifts are staffed roughly equally; the slight imbalance is reflected in the observation allocation. - If actual staffing differs, recalculate the % of staff per shift and re‑allocate observations proportionally (e.g., 40 × (shift nurses ÷ total nurses)). **Scheduling details** 1. **Random sampling within each shift** – auditors use a simple random list of patient rooms or nursing stations for each observation day. 2. **Observation cadence** – each auditor performs ~20 observations per month (10 in two shifts, 10 in the third) to keep workload manageable and maintain consistency across days. 3. **Shift‑specific audit windows** – Auditor A covers morning & night; Auditor B covers evening. This allows each auditor to become familiar with the workflow of their assigned shift. --- **2. What an auditor must record for a *valid* observation** | Field | Description (WHO Five Moments) | Why it matters | |-------|---------------------------------|----------------| | **Date & time** | Exact timestamp of the encounter | Enables trend analysis and shift‑level comparison | | **Shift identifier** | Morning / Evening / Night | Links compliance to staffing patterns | | **Nurse ID or badge number** (anonymised if required) | Unique identifier | Allows follow‑up training for specific staff | | **Patient room/area** | Location of the encounter | Detects location‑based gaps | | **Procedure type** | e.g., medication administration, wound care, routine check | Contextualises hand‑hygiene need | | **Five Moments checklist** – for each moment:
• Moment number (1–5)
• Action performed? (Yes/No)
• Product used (soap & water / alcohol‑based rub)
• Correct technique observed? | Captures compliance at the granular level | Enables targeted feedback | | **Observer ID** | Auditor A or B | Tracks inter‑observer reliability | | **Notes/comments** | Brief narrative of any barriers, environmental issues, or deviations | Provides qualitative insight | *Validity criteria:* - All five moments must be evaluated for each encounter. - The observation must be made *unobtrusively* (i.e., the nurse is unaware that they are being observed) to avoid Hawthorne bias. - The auditor must complete the form within 5 minutes of the encounter to preserve accuracy. --- **3. Presenting monthly results** | Format | Content | Visualisation | |--------|---------|---------------| | **Dashboard (digital or printed)** | • Overall compliance rate = (compliant moments ÷ total moments observed) × 100%
• Shift‑level rates
• Moment‑by‑moment breakdown
• Top 3 rooms/areas with lowest compliance | Bar chart for shift comparison; stacked bar for moment distribution | | **Summary table** | Rows: Morning, Evening, Night, Overall. Columns: # observations, # moments observed, # compliant moments, % compliance. | Simple tabular view for quick reference | | **Trend line (if multi‑month)** | Monthly compliance over the past 6 months | Line graph to show improvement or regression | | **Action‑plan section** | • Highlight moments with < 80 % compliance
• Assign targeted training sessions
• Review environmental factors (e.g., hand‑rub station placement) | Bullet points under each low‑performing area | *Reporting cadence:* - **Monthly meeting** – present the dashboard to unit leadership and nursing staff. - **Follow‑up email** – share a concise PDF with key metrics and next steps. --- ### What could change this conclusion? | Factor | Impact | |--------|--------| | **Shift staffing variance** | If one shift has significantly more nurses, re‑allocate observations proportionally to maintain representativeness. | | **Audit scope expansion** | Adding additional moments (e.g., after glove removal) would increase the number of data points per observation and could alter compliance percentages. | | **Regulatory updates** | Local health authority mandates may require different hand‑hygiene metrics; adjust the audit form accordingly. | *Note:* This plan is based on WHO’s Five Moments framework as understood up to my training cut‑off in 2024. If newer guidelines have been issued since then, they should be incorporated into the observation checklist and reporting logic.
